narrative.overview: FerrisTrace is the room a team walks into when production misbehaves. Everything is visible at a glance and nothing raises its voice except what is broken. The system is dense but ordered: small strict type, tabular numbers, flat panels separated by hairline borders. Two people use this room with equal weight: the developer paged at night on a phone, and the SRE who lives in it all day on a wide screen.
keyCharacteristics: Quiet neutrals, one accent, colour reserved for state.
Flat surfaces, hairline borders, shadows only on floating layers.
Small, strict type scale; tabular numbers; monospace for identifiers and values.
Light and dark themes, both first-class.
Problems rank first and carry the only loud colour on the screen.

rules.name: The Only Loud Thing Rule
rules.body: Red and amber appear only where something is broken or degrading. If nothing is wrong, the screen has no saturated colour besides the indigo accent.

rules.name: The Green Is An Answer Rule
rules.body: Green marks health only where the user asked "is it fine?" (a status, a check). Rows that are simply running stay neutral.

rules.name: The Machine Wrote It Rule
rules.body: Anything a system produced (ids, hashes, durations, timestamps, query text) is set in mono with tabular figures; anything a person reads as prose is set in the sans.

rules.name: The Flat Room Rule
rules.body: A card at rest has a border and no shadow. Depth means "this floats above the page", nothing else.

dos: Do rank problems first in every list and give them the only saturated colour on screen.
Do set ids, durations, timestamps and values in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
Do separate surfaces with hairline borders (border) and one-step tonal shifts.
Do keep touch targets at 44px or more on phones, and inputs at 16px on touch devices.
Do design both themes; check every state colour against card in light and dark.
donts: Don't put a shadow on a card at rest; shadows are for floating layers only.
Don't paint healthy or merely running items green; neutral is the default for "nothing to see".
Don't introduce a second accent hue in the app; the extra accents (teal, orange, rose, slate) belong to the public status page only.
Don't use primary as a chart fill; use series.
Don't present mock or missing data as real; say what is unknown.
